# X360 Mobile 0.6.4

This update moves X360 Mobile to a newer Xenia Edge core, with a refreshed Android interface, new ways to play and share compatibility results, and further work on game compatibility and performance.

## New features

- Optional frame interpolation for smoother displayed motion, with automatic and per-game controls.
- Experimental TV mode with larger game covers, top-tab controller navigation and external-display selection.
- X360 Mobile Live Lobbies for supported System Link games: direct LAN/Internet connections, public or friends-only rooms, optional passwords, invitations, chat, friend requests and friend presence. Two-console co-op has been checked in Gears of War.
- Experimental synchronized player profiles using X360 Mobile website accounts, with achievement and Gamerscore synchronization across devices.
- Automatic discovery of games added to registered library folders, without requiring another manual scan.
- Local autocomplete suggestions in the Xbox-style keyboard for installed games and settings searches.
- Configurable controller button combinations and quick-menu favorites, with separate global and per-game preferences.
- Disc-change prompts can suggest a matching disc from the current folder for quick loading, while retaining manual browsing.
- Optional Samsung performance controls and per-game support for compatible graphics layers, including ExynosTools/MdiEx packages.

## Interface, controls and everyday use

- Updated app branding and startup presentation, with a new boot video, splash transition and app icon.
- Refreshed adaptive layouts for different mobile aspect ratios, display cutouts and large screens.
- Menus and editors stay within the content area, keeping navigation and the contextual hintbar available.
- Refreshed achievement notification styling.
- Cover-sized game cards, compact on-cover controls and favorites indicators, clearer home/library organization, and contextual controller hints.
- Artwork display modes for disc art, cover art or cover art with fallback; clearer refresh controls and snoozable provider-limit notices.
- Improved navigation preserves searches, selections and scroll positions when returning from settings and nested pages.
- Expanded performance overlay with optional CPU/RAM information, available device GPU metrics and selectable temperature sources. Temperature values now use a compact display without sensor-name annotations.
- Broader English, Italian, German, French, Spanish and Brazilian Portuguese coverage across Android screens, native menus and setting descriptions.
- Refined experimental phone vibration with gentler effects and separate intensity controls.
- Expanded integration with ES-DE, Daijishō, Beacon, Retro Hrai and Cocoon Shell.
- Guided import of supported library and touch-layout data from the previous app.
- Clearer content/driver cleanup confirmations and safer handling of unrelated games, saves and settings.

## Compatibility reports and community features

- Rebuilt opt-in compatibility reporting with four playability ratings, reviewable local drafts, recovery of interrupted sessions and scheduled uploads.
- Reports are organized by game, with batch deletion and manual per-game reporting exclusions.
- Reports retain configuration details and separate results when settings change during a session. Uploads are deferred while a game is running.
- Compatibility pages on the website retain individual session reports and existing community data, with hardware, driver and app-version filters and expandable configuration details.
- Report authors can add descriptive notes and clarify driver names while preserving the original measurements. Administration includes correction history and batch moderation tools.

## Core, game fixes and performance

- General compatibility and performance work across graphics, shaders, runtime timing, storage, audio and input in the updated core.
- Startup and loading improvements affecting Naruto: Rise of a Ninja, Metro 2033, Wolfenstein: The New Order and Peter Jackson's King Kong.
- Stability, rendering and performance improvements for Need for Speed: The Run, with optional visual adjustments.
- Performance and timing work checked in Ninety-Nine Nights and Naruto: Rise of a Ninja, with stutter improvements in tested Assassin's Creed scenes.
- Rendering improvements for BioShock 2, and rendering/runtime stability improvements for Fable II.
- Rendering improvements for Viva Piñata, plus an optional experimental stability patch.
- Audio fixes checked in Blood Drive and Grand Theft Auto V, with clearer required-update guidance for GTA V.
- Partial rendering improvements and compatibility profiles for Splinter Cell Conviction, Blue Dragon, Rise of the Tomb Raider and Spider-Man: Shattered Dimensions. Splinter Cell Conviction also received performance work in tested scenes.
- Improved startup, pause/resume, session shutdown and shader-cache reliability.
- Reduced unnecessary background and overlay work, with a dedicated Power and thermal settings section and optional efficiency controls.

## Important notes

- TV mode and synchronized player profiles are still highly experimental and may have bugs or reliability issues.
- Some game improvements require the appropriate compatibility settings or supported graphics features. Results vary by game, scene, device and driver.
- Assassin's Creed still has an unresolved GPU crash. Blue Dragon, Wolfenstein: The New Order and Rise of the Tomb Raider retain known visual issues; Splinter Cell Conviction improvements remain partial.
- Frame interpolation smooths displayed motion; guest simulation speed is unchanged. GPU cost and input latency depend on the chosen settings.
- Live Lobbies supports System Link games rather than Xbox Live services. Direct Internet connections depend on network conditions; relay fallback is not included.
- Sensor readings, Samsung controls and graphics-layer compatibility depend on the device and package version. Some original texture-layer packages still have known compatibility issues. Custom graphics packages are not bundled with the app.
- Achievement synchronization does not provide cloud save synchronization. Compatibility reporting remains optional.
